the heptapeptidal angiotensin AIII modulated the interactive effect of nociception and hypertension on the responsiveness of NRGC medullary neurons in the anesthetized rat.

angiotensin II and its heptapeptide metabolite, angiotensin (1-7) (angiotensin (AIII)) modulate nociception-related neuronal responsiveness in nucleus reticularis (NRGC), a key brainstem structure that is involved in cardiovascular regulation.

angiotensin (Ang) III, an octapeptide that is a member of a family of biologically active peptides known as angiotensin, modulates the responsiveness of neurons located in the nucleus reticulularis gigantocellulais (NRGC) in the rat brainstem to noxious stimuli (nociception) and elevation in systemic blood pressure (hypertension).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role played by the central nervous system (CNS) in the integration of cardiovascular and nociceptive reflexes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

AIII is a modulatory peptide that is capable of selectively altering the responsiveness of NRGC cells to nociception and hypertension, depending on whether the two stimuli are presented individually or simultaneously.
the heptapeptide modulates nociception-related neuronal responsiveness in NRGC, and that it does so by a receptor-mediated mechanism.
AIII, through its receptor(s), can differentially modulate the responsiveness of neurons to different physiologic inputs, and that this modulation may be dependent on the nature of the inputs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heptapeptides may have a role in the integration of nociceptive and arterial pressure-related information in the NRGC.
the heptapeptidic angiotensin is a modulator that may play an important role in the central integration of cardiovascular and nociceptive information.
AIII is a neuromodulator that can alter the interactive effect of nociception and elevation in arterial pressure on the excitability of neurons in the NRGC of the medulla.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain's ability to integrate and respond appropriately to the simultaneous occurrence of two physiologic stimuli may not be as rigidly fixed as previously assumed.
AIII may be involved in the regulation of nociception and/or hypertension in the central nervous system.
AIII may be a key modulator of neuronal responsiveness in the central nervous system.
